title: Day in, day out
goals: Say and understand the time (It's a quarter after six).
Talk about how often you do something (I rarely have free time, twice a week).
Say when you do something with on / at / in (on Fridays, at 6 p.m., in the morning).
Order actions in your routine with before, after, until.
Describe your day in a short paragraph using complete sentences (subject + verb).
Understand descriptions of jobs and routines (a roadie, a TV journalist).

learn.title: Saying the time
learn.html:
To ask and say what time it is, there are two ways: with numbers (six fifteen) and with words (a quarter after six). The answer always starts with It's.

QuestionAnswerVariation
What time is it?It's nine o'clock.It's nine.
Excuse me, what time is it?It's a quarter after six.It's six fifteen.
—It's twenty after eight.It's eight twenty.
—It's five thirty.It's half past five.
  • For "at six o'clock", use at: The class starts at six.
  • American English uses after (British English uses past): ten after seven = ten past seven.
  • For the minutes before the hour, use to: a quarter to twelve (11:45).

watch.why: Telling the time uses It's (subject it).

watch.wrong: I get up in the six.
watch.why: Use at with clock times, with no article.

learn.title: Frequency adverbs and adverb phrases
learn.html:
Used to say how often you do something. From most to least: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never.

SituationAdverb positionExample
Verb beafter beHe is never late. / We are always at home.
Other verbsbefore the verbYolanda rarely watches TV.
Frases (once a week, three times a week, every day)at the end of the sentenceClare drives to work three times a week.

Useful equivalents: every day ≈ always; once a year ≈ rarely; about once a month ≈ sometimes; doesn't … on Sundays ≈ never.

watch.why: With be, the adverb goes after be.

watch.wrong: Always I eat with my friends.
watch.right: I always eat with my friends.
watch.why: The adverb goes before the verb, not at the beginning.

watch.wrong: I go always to the gym.
watch.right: I always go to the gym.
watch.why: The adverb goes before the main verb.

learn.title: Time prepositions: on / at / in
learn.html:
Used to say when something happens.

PrepositionUsed withExamples
ondays, and weekdays / the weekend (American English)on Wednesday, on Fridays, on weekdays, on the weekend
atclock times, noon, midnight, nightat four o'clock, at midnight, at night
inparts of the dayin the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening

British English also says at the weekend.

learn.title: Clauses with before, after, until
learn.html:
Used to put two actions in order in time. Each word is followed by a full clause (subject + verb).

WordMeaningExampleOrder of events
beforebefore that happensI have a shower before I go swimming.1) shower, 2) swim
afterafter that happensThe bus comes after the train leaves.1) the train leaves, 2) the bus arrives
untiluntil that happensI study until my class starts.I study for the whole time before class starts
  • The clause can go at the start (with a comma) or at the end (no comma): Before she cooks, Jen washes her hands. / Jen washes her hands before she cooks.
  • To join two sentences: I cook. Then my wife washes the dishes. → After I cook, my wife washes the dishes.

watch.wrong: He takes a shower after has breakfast.
watch.right: He takes a shower after he has breakfast.
watch.why: After after, before or until, use subject + verb.

watch.wrong: I study until to ten o'clock.

learn.title: Writing: every sentence needs a subject and a verb
learn.html:
In English the subject is almost never left out, even when it seems obvious (for example, "He arrives at eight", not "Arrives at eight").

SubjectVerbExample
name / pronoun (Toshihiko, He, We)starts, is, go, buyToshihiko starts work at seven thirty.
It (time, weather)isIt is sunny today. / It's five o'clock.

Example of a full paragraph: After work, he goes to his English class. Before he goes home, he goes to a café. After dinner, he does his homework until it is time to go to sleep.

watch.right: After work, he goes to class.
watch.why: The subject is missing after the opening phrase.
home takes no to with movement verbs.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• Excuse me, what time is it? — to ask a stranger for the time.
  • It's time to go home! — to say that it's time to leave.
  • I rarely have free time. — to say that you are very busy.
  • Then, … / After that, … — to link activities when you talk about your day.
  • At 12 p.m., I … until 5 p.m. — to describe a block of time.
  • Time flies when you are having fun. — to say that time went by fast.

write.prompt: Write 6 to 8 sentences about your work or study day. Include: two times (at … o'clock), three frequency adverbs (one with be), one sentence with before, one with after and one with until. Use Then or After that to link ideas. Starter: I usually get up at six thirty. Before I have breakfast, I …
targets: subject and verb in each sentence
checklist: Two times with at (at six o'clock)
Three frequency adverbs, one with be (I am never late)
Adverb after be and before other verbs
One sentence with before, one with after and one with until, each with subject + verb
Correct on / at / in (on Mondays, at night, in the morning)
Subject in each sentence; I go home (no to)
Then or After that to link ideas
write.model: I usually get up at six thirty. Before I have breakfast, I take a shower. Then I go to work. I am never late, and I start work at eight o'clock. I sometimes have lunch with my friends. I work until the office closes. After I finish work, I go home. On Mondays, I go to the gym in the evening.

reading.title: A busy day in Guadalajara
paragraphs: Hi! I'm Valeria and I work in a bank in Guadalajara. My day is busy. I always get up at six fifteen. Before I have breakfast, I take a shower. I take the bus to work and I start at eight o'clock. In the morning, I answer emails until noon. I usually have my lunch break at one o'clock, and I sometimes go for a walk in the park. I finish work at five thirty.

On Tuesdays and Thursdays, I work out in the gym. On Fridays, I go dancing with my friends. On the weekend, I rarely get up early. I often ride my bike on Sunday mornings. I never go to bed late. After I have dinner, I watch TV until ten o'clock. Then I go to bed. My life is busy, but I love it!

It's a quarter after eight. Why?
My English class starts at nine. I usually take the bus, but it's always late.
Do you have class every day?
No, I have class three times a week. On Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.
I go to the gym on Tuesdays. I work out until seven thirty in the evening.
Wow! Do you go on weekends too?

That sounds nice. I never get up late.
